bugs.error_message: Error from server: Get "https://<node-ip>:10250/containerLogs/...": No agent available -- every kubectl logs/exec/port-forward on the homelab k0s cluster
bugs.root_cause: k0s konnectivity agents all dial exactly ONE address: spec.api.externalAddress when set, otherwise whichever controller's own spec.api.address won the race to write the konnectivity-agent DaemonSet (k0sproject/k0s#600, #5503). bootstrap-k0s-cluster.sh never set externalAddress, so on the 3-controller cluster all agents pinned to k0s-02 (192.0.2.10) while fetch_kubeconfig rewrote the kubeconfig server to k0s-01's Tailscale IP -- kubectl therefore hit an API server with zero agents registered. `kubectl get` kept working because it never leaves etcd, which masked the failure until an OSArtifact builder pod needed its logs read.
bugs.fix: Emit spec.api.externalAddress (default: first controller's INTERNAL DHCP address, so in-cluster traffic stays on the libvirt network) and force it into spec.api.sans. Rewrite only the kubeconfig's `server:` line, to the Tailscale IP of that SAME node, so kubectl and the konnectivity agents converge on one API server. New API_EXTERNAL_ADDRESS / KUBECONFIG_SERVER overrides + matching K0S_* Makefile vars. Requires a cluster rebuild -- externalAddress is baked in at init.

bugs.error_message: make k0s-remote-destroy reports success but VMs remain defined (visible in Cockpit, 'shut off'); underlying: 'error: Requested operation is not valid: cannot undefine domain with nvram'
bugs.root_cause: destroy_all ran `virsh destroy` (force power-off only) then `virsh undefine --remove-all-storage`, with BOTH piped to /dev/null 2>&1 || true. The undefine failed for two stacked reasons: (1) create_vm uses --boot uefi so each domain has an <nvram> varstore, and libvirt 11.3.0 still requires an explicit --nvram/--keep-nvram to undefine such a domain; (2) --remove-all-storage cannot resolve the per-VM qcow2/seed.iso because they live in a SUBDIRECTORY of the pool -- `vol-list default` manages only the k0s-bootstrap directory itself as one volume, not the files inside -- so the whole undefine aborts. Error swallowing hid both. Compounding: create_vm short-circuits on any already-defined domain (dominfo ok -> just start it), so the next `all` run silently reused the stale VMs.
bugs.fix: undefine now passes `--nvram --managed-save` and drops --remove-all-storage (the qcow2/seed ISO are rm -f'd directly two lines later anyway). Errors are surfaced + set failed=1 instead of `|| true`, and a post-teardown verification re-lists domains matching ^$VM_PREFIX-[0-9]+$ and exits 1 if any survive. Regex verified not to match unrelated hypervisor domains (win11, ubuntu-lab, k0s-bootstrap-helper, k0svm).

bugs.error_message: PVC smoke-test-artifacts stuck Pending: 'no persistent volumes available for this claim and no storage class is set'; local-path-provisioner pod Pending 12h with '0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had untolerated taint(s)'
bugs.root_cause: Two stacked. (1) k0s taints controller+worker nodes node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule by default; with ALL 3 nodes controller+worker nothing schedulable can run, so local-path-provisioner never started. (2) kairos-operator creates each OSArtifact's PVC with NO storageClassName, so it binds to the cluster default AT CREATION TIME -- the smoke-test PVC was created before any default StorageClass existed, so storageClassName was permanently '' and, being immutable, the claim can never bind even after a default is added. Also the `kubectl patch storageclass ... is-default-class` step had silently not landed (annotations showed only last-applied-configuration).
bugs.fix: bootstrap-k0s-cluster.sh emits `noTaints: true` on controller+worker hosts (NO_TAINTS override, default true; K0S_NO_TAINTS in the Makefile). New bootstrap-kairos-operator.sh enforces the ordering: preflight-fail if every node is NoSchedule-tainted, install storage, claim default only if none exists, VERIFY the default annotation, wait for the provisioner to be Available, then install the operator, and only then create an OSArtifact -- deleting any prior OSArtifact AND its PVC first so an unbindable legacy claim is never reused.

bugs.error_message: preflight_scheduling returned exit=0 (check passed) on a cluster where all 3 nodes WERE NoSchedule-tainted
bugs.root_cause: In a kubectl go-template, `$` is the template ROOT (the List object), not the current range item. `{{range .items}}{{range .spec.taints}}...{{$.metadata.name}}` therefore emitted the List's (empty) metadata.name -> literally '<no value>' per tainted node. `sort -u` collapsed those three identical lines to one, so tainted=1 while total=3, and the `tainted -eq total` guard never fired.
bugs.fix: Capture the node name into a variable inside the outer range before descending: `{{range .items}}{{$n := .metadata.name}}{{range .spec.taints}}{{if eq .effect "NoSchedule"}}{{$n}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}{{end}}{{end}}`. Verified against the live cluster: broken form printed '<no value>' x3 (count 1), fixed form printed k0s-01/02/03 (count 3).

bugs.error_message: k0sctl apply failed: 'ssh: handshake failed: host key mismatch: knownhosts: key mismatch' / 'retrying aborted ... abort condition reached after 1 attempts' for 192.0.2.10
bugs.root_cause: k0sctl uses its own SSH stack (the rig library) which reads ~/.ssh/known_hosts directly. It does NOT inherit the `-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null` that the script's own ssh_run sets, and k0sctl v0.32.1 has no flag to relax host-key checking. libvirt recycles its DHCP pool across destroy/create cycles, so a recreated VM gets an IP whose host key is still pinned from a PREVIOUS VM -- k0sctl then aborts the whole apply after one attempt. Confirmed on the hypervisor: 192.0.2.10 pinned at line 51 of root's known_hosts (hashed entry).
bugs.fix: New purge_known_hosts() helper; apply_k0sctl now runs `ssh-keygen -R <ip>` for every host address parsed out of the generated k0sctl.yaml (awk '$1=="address:"') before calling k0sctl apply. Reading addresses from the config file (not a variable) keeps a standalone `apply` working. ssh-keygen -R is required rather than grep/sed because the entries are hashed. Verified the awk extraction returns exactly the 3 ssh.address values and does not match externalAddress.

bugs.error_message: OSArtifact phase=Error; init container pull-image-baseimage: 'failed to unpack image: ... GET https://quay.io/v2/kairos/ubuntu/manifests/24.04-standard-amd64-generic-v3.6.0: MANIFEST_UNKNOWN: manifest unknown'
bugs.root_cause: The image tag quay.io/kairos/ubuntu:24.04-standard-amd64-generic-v3.6.0 does not exist and never did. It was copied verbatim out of an earlier disconnected prototype's docs and propagated into 7 places (script default, example YAML, two guides, three unit-test fixtures) WITHOUT ever being resolved against the registry -- the same failure mode as that prototype's invented Helm chart names. Kairos tags are <os>-<flavor>-<arch>-<model>-<kairos-version>, and a `standard` tag ALWAYS carries a bundled k8s distro suffix (e.g. -k0s-v1.34.3-k0s.0); a bare `24.04-standard-amd64-generic-vX.Y.Z` is not a real shape. Verified via quay v2 API: bad tag -> HTTP 404, 24.04-core-amd64-generic-v3.7.2 -> 200, 24.04-standard-amd64-generic-v3.7.2-k0s-v1.34.3-k0s.0 -> 200.
bugs.fix: Replaced all 7 occurrences with registry-verified tags: `core` (no bundled k8s) for the smoke test + operator-setup guide, `standard`+k0s for the banlieue VMImage example + its guide. Added a docs admonition covering the core-vs-standard tag grammar and a copy-pasteable quay v2 manifest HEAD check, since the failure mode is expensive (surfaces only after a ~570MB builder-image pull) and the real error is buried in an INIT container's logs.

bugs.error_message: OSArtifact build-cloud-image: 'failed to create recovery image error="open /dev/loop0: no such file or directory"' / 'gen-raw-efi-disk (error: open /dev/loop0: no such file or directory)'
bugs.root_cause: Startup race, not permissions. The builder container IS privileged:true (verified on the pod spec), but a privileged container only receives host device NODES that existed at container-creation time. The kernel `loop` module is not loaded at boot on a stock Debian cloud image; it autoloads on first /dev/loop-control access -- which is the builder itself. So the container opened /dev/loop-control (present), the kernel autoloaded loop and created /dev/loop0..7 ON THE HOST a moment later, but the container's already-populated /dev never saw them. Proven by comparing nodes: only k0s-02 (which ran the build) had the module loaded + 8 loop devices, timestamped at the exact build minute; k0s-01 and k0s-03 had neither. Insidious follow-on: a SECOND build on the same node would succeed, making it look intermittent.
bugs.fix: cloud-init now writes /etc/modules-load.d/loop.conf (content: loop) so the module loads at every boot, plus `modprobe loop` in runcmd so the first boot needs no reboot. Restructured make_cloud_init_files so the single permitted cloud-config `runcmd` key is assembled in one place (tailscale previously owned it exclusively). Validated by rendering the user-data with and without TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY and parsing both as YAML. Also added a signature-matching HINT to bootstrap-kairos-operator.sh's smoke_diagnostics for both this and the MANIFEST_UNKNOWN case.

bugs.error_message: bootstrap-libvirt-tls.sh: 'Job failed. See journalctl -xe' -- systemd: 'libvirtd-tls.socket: Socket service libvirtd.service already active, refusing.'
bugs.root_cause: systemd refuses to start a .socket unit whose corresponding service is ALREADY RUNNING. configure_libvirtd() called `systemctl enable --now libvirtd-tls.socket` while libvirtd.service had 1d13h uptime, so it failed every time; with `set -e` the script aborted there, before restarting libvirtd, before verify(), and before write_secret() (so no Secret manifest was produced). Second, related defect: `systemctl disable --now libvirtd-tcp.socket` does NOT close port 16509 on a running daemon, because libvirtd keeps serving the socket fd it already inherited -- confirmed, 16509 still LISTENing on pid 1411 fd=6 after the 'disable'.
bugs.fix: Re-armed socket activation in the correct order: stop libvirtd.service, stop ALL libvirtd*.socket units, disable libvirtd-tcp.socket, enable libvirtd-tls.socket, start the desired socket set, then start libvirtd.service. Both `systemctl start` calls are now checked and fail loudly with the exact journalctl command instead of being swallowed.

bugs.error_message: libvirtd.conf ended up with DUPLICATE active settings after bootstrap-libvirt-tls.sh: listen_tls/listen_tcp each present twice (lines 22+537, 38+538), and a commented doc example silently turned into live config
bugs.root_cause: set_conf()'s grep/sed patterns included an optional comment marker (`^\s*#?\s*KEY\s*=`). libvirtd.conf documents every option as a COMMENTED example (e.g. `#listen_tls = 0` at line 22) hundreds of lines above the file's real settings (line 537). The `#?` therefore matched the documentation, and because sed had no address restriction it rewrote EVERY match -- uncommenting the prose into an active setting and leaving two live copies of the same key. Verified against the .pre-banlieue-tls backup: line 22 went `#listen_tls = 0` -> `listen_tls = 1`. Benign only because both copies received the same value; two contradictory active settings on any future run with a different value.
bugs.fix: Dropped `#?` from both patterns so only ACTIVE settings are matched; when no active setting exists the key is appended instead of a doc example being uncommented. Verified with a fixture containing both a commented example and a real setting: exactly one active key results, the doc example stays commented, and an absent key is appended.

bugs.error_message: banlieue-libvirt XDR: Decoder::read_opaque_fixed(usize::MAX) panics with 'attempt to add with overflow' in debug; in release len+pad WRAPS to a small value, passing the bounds check and then corrupting self.pos
bugs.root_cause: read_opaque_fixed computed `len + pad` unchecked. `len` is public API input AND is fed straight from a wire-read u32 by read_opaque_var. padding_for(usize::MAX) == 1, so usize::MAX + 1 overflows: debug panics, release wraps to 0 -> `self.remaining() < 0` is false -> the guard passes -> `self.pos += len` corrupts the cursor. Found by MUTATION TESTING, not by the test suite: deleting the redundant bounds check in read_opaque_var left all 21 tests green (the inner check in read_opaque_fixed still caught the 64-bit case), which prompted a look at why the inner check was load-bearing and exposed the overflow.
bugs.fix: Use `len.checked_add(pad).ok_or(XdrError::UnexpectedEof)?`. Added a regression test (read_opaque_fixed_rejects_length_that_overflows_when_padded) and verified via mutation that it FAILS with unchecked `+` and passes with checked_add.

bugs.error_message: banlieue-libvirt procs: connect_open(read_only=true) could silently open a READ-WRITE connection and every test still passed
bugs.root_cause: Test gap, not a code defect. `encode_connect_open_args(None, CONNECT_RO)` was asserted in isolation, but nothing asserted that `connect_open(.., read_only: true)` actually PLUMBS CONNECT_RO into the args it sends. Mutation testing exposed it: replacing `let flags = if read_only { CONNECT_RO } else { 0 };` with `let flags = 0;` left all 60 tests green. A silent downgrade from read-only to read-write is a least-privilege failure that would never have surfaced in review.
bugs.fix: Added `connect_open_plumbs_read_only_through_to_the_wire`, which drives connect_open over a scripted duplex peer and asserts the ARGUMENT BYTES that actually reached the peer equal encode_connect_open_args(uri, CONNECT_RO) — and, for read_only=false, equal the flags-0 encoding. Verified the new test FAILS under the original mutation and passes with correct code; the procedures layer now catches 6/6 mutations. General lesson: testing an encoder in isolation does not test that callers use it correctly — assert on what reaches the wire.

bugs.error_message: procs::procs_tests::tests::connect_open_plumbs_read_only_through_to_the_wire panicked: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Xdr(UnexpectedEof) — at crates/banlieue-libvirt/src/procs_tests.rs:204
bugs.root_cause: NOT YET DIAGNOSED — intermittent. Failed once during `cargo test --all`, then passed 11/11 runs of the test alone and of `cargo test -p banlieue-libvirt --lib`, and 4/4 further `cargo test --all` runs. Reproduces only under whole-workspace parallelism, so the suspicion is a timing/ordering assumption in the mock byte-stream the test reads from (an UnexpectedEof means the reader observed a short read), not a defect in `procs.rs` itself. Unrelated to the ADR-0012 operator work — that touched no file in banlieue-libvirt except the &PathBuf->&Path lint fix in tests/live_libvirtd.rs.
bugs.fix: NOT FIXED. Logged so the next occurrence is recognised as recurring rather than new. When it reappears: run with `--test-threads=1` to confirm it is a concurrency artefact, and check whether the test's duplex/mock stream can return a partial read that the decoder treats as EOF instead of retrying.

bugs.error_message: banlieue-libvirt: connect_tls succeeded ('TLS established') but the first RPC never returned — hung indefinitely with no error from either side; libvirtd logged nothing
bugs.root_cause: libvirt's TLS transport has a mandatory post-handshake step that appears in NO protocol document — only in libvirt's own client source (src/rpc/virnetclient.c): after the TLS handshake the server validates the client certificate and source address and, if satisfied, sends a single 0x01 byte. Its comment: 'At this point, the server is verifying _our_ certificate, IP address, etc. If we make the grade, it will send us a \1 byte.' We never read it, so the byte stayed in the receive buffer; the first reply's 4-byte length prefix was then parsed one byte out of alignment, producing a garbage length, and read_exact blocked forever waiting for bytes that would never arrive. Fails silently by construction: libvirtd answered correctly and logged nothing, and TLS/auth/framing were all individually correct.
bugs.fix: After the handshake in connect_tls, read exactly one byte and require it to equal 0x01, else return TransportError::Tls describing a server-side rejection of our certificate or source address. Verified against the live host: CONNECT_OPEN now returns and LIST_ALL_STORAGE_POOLS decodes 4 pools whose names and UUIDs match `virsh pool-list`/`pool-info` exactly.

bugs.error_message: banlieue-libvirt: CONNECT_OPEN sent as the first message on a session; real libvirt clients always send AUTH_LIST (proc 66) first
bugs.root_cause: The client jumped straight to CONNECT_OPEN. A real client traced with `LIBVIRT_DEBUG=1 virsh list` shows its first message is proc=66 (REMOTE_PROC_AUTH_LIST), serial=0, len=28 — authentication negotiation precedes CONNECT_OPEN on every connection. The same trace also disproved the documentation on serials: libvirt's RPC kbase says serials 'start at 1', but the reference client sends serial=0 first and serial=1 second.
bugs.fix: Added PROC_AUTH_LIST (66), an AuthType enum (None/Sasl/Polkit/Unknown), decode_auth_list, and auth_list(). connect_open() now negotiates first and refuses with TransportError::Protocol if REMOTE_AUTH_NONE is not offered (banlieue supports x509 client-cert auth only). Session serials now start at 0 to match the reference implementation rather than its prose. Unit tests updated; the two-call handshake required rewriting the scripted-peer helper to answer AUTH_LIST before capturing the call under test.

bugs.error_message: providers.banlieue.io "e2e-vc" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:banlieue-system:banlieue-operator" cannot patch resource "providers" in API group "banlieue.io" in the namespace "banlieue-e2e" — every Provider reconcile 403'd, no workload was ever created
bugs.root_cause: Conflated two DIFFERENT Kubernetes permissions. The operator ClusterRole granted `update` on `providers/finalizers` and assumed that covered adding its `banlieue.io/provider-workload` finalizer. It does not. `<resource>/finalizers` is the admission-time permission the apiserver requires before it will accept a DEPENDENT carrying `ownerReference.blockOwnerDeletion: true`. Writing `metadata.finalizers` on the object itself is an ordinary write to the MAIN resource and needs update/patch on `providers`. The reconciler calls ensure_finalizer() before anything else, so every reconcile failed at the first step and retried every 5s forever.
bugs.fix: Added a rule granting update/patch on `providers` (kept separate from the /status and /finalizers rules, each with a comment explaining which permission it is and why). Added two unit guards in bootstrap_tests.rs that parse the embedded ClusterRole: operator_cluster_role_can_write_the_provider_finalizer and operator_cluster_role_can_set_block_owner_deletion.

bugs.error_message: e2e test `a_paused_provider_gets_no_workload` PASSED while the operator was completely broken (every reconcile 403ing) — a false green
bugs.root_cause: The test asserted only the ABSENCE of a workload after pausing a Provider. Absence is satisfied just as well by an operator that is dead, crash-looping, or 403ing on every reconcile, so the assertion carried no information. It passed on the very run where bug-104 made the operator entirely non-functional.
bugs.fix: After asserting absence, the test now unpauses the Provider (merge patch spec.paused=false) and waits for the workload to actually appear. That establishes the operator was alive and willing, which is what makes the absence check meaningful. General rule: an assertion that something did NOT happen needs a paired positive control, or it is untestable-by-construction.

bugs.error_message: unexpected argument '--provider-name' found (banlieue provider libvirt would crash-loop under the operator)
bugs.root_cause: banlieue-operator's build_args() emits --provider-name for EVERY backend, but only the vSphere Cli declared that flag. A libvirt Provider created through the operator produced a Deployment whose container failed clap parsing at startup and never reached a reconcile. Unit tests on either side passed: the operator tested that it emits the flag, the provider tested the flags it declares, and nothing tested that the two agree.
bugs.fix: Added --provider-name (env BANLIEUE_PROVIDER_NAME) to the libvirt Cli plus provider_watch_config() to narrow the watch server-side, matching vSphere. Added a test asserting the operator-supplied flag parses.

bugs.error_message: import Job would exec `banlieue provider libvirt import`, a subcommand that did not exist
bugs.root_cause: The VMImage reconciler's Job manifest was written against a CLI surface that was never implemented. Every unit test asserted on the manifest as JSON, so nothing ever fed those args to a parser.
bugs.fix: Implemented the import subcommand (volume_name/find_pool/plan/source_length + run). Added a round-trip test that takes the argv out of the generated Job manifest and parses it through the real clap parser, so manifest and CLI cannot drift apart silently again.

bugs.error_message: examples/02-provider-libvirt-edge.yaml used qemu+ssh:// and had no caBundle
bugs.root_cause: The example predates ADR-0011's TLS-only decision. parse_endpoint() explicitly rejects any scheme other than qemu+tls, and credentials::resolve() requires caBundle, so anyone following the example got Ready=False on first reconcile.
bugs.fix: Switched to qemu+tls:// with a caBundle.configMapRef, and documented the whole flow in docs/src/guides/libvirt-provider.md.

bugs.error_message: clusterrolebindings ... forbidden: banlieue-operator is attempting to grant RBAC permissions not currently held: {APIGroups:[""], Resources:["secrets"], Verbs:["list" "watch"]}
bugs.root_cause: The shared per-backend provider ClusterRole granted secrets/configmaps get+list+watch. It is attached with a ClusterRoleBinding, so list/watch means read EVERY Secret in the cluster — silently defeating the resourceNames narrowing that per-instance topology (ADR-0003) exists to provide. It also blocked the operator from creating the binding at all, since RBAC refuses to let a grantor hand out permissions it does not hold.
bugs.fix: Narrowed to `get` on secrets and configmaps: every call site (reconciler/provider.rs, vmimage.rs, ca_bundle.rs) reads by name via api.get(name), so list/watch bought nothing. The tempting fix — widening the operator ClusterRole to match — would have PROPAGATED the over-grant instead of removing it. Guarded by no_provider_cluster_role_grants_blanket_secret_enumeration, which iterates every backend.

bugs.error_message: Provider workload never functional: the ClusterRoleBinding the operator creates referenced ClusterRole banlieue-provider-<backend>, which nothing had installed
bugs.root_cause: build_operator_install installed ClusterRoles for the Controller and Operator roles only. The operator BINDS the shared per-backend provider ClusterRole to every per-instance ServiceAccount but cannot create it (minting the permissions it hands out is the escalation path ADR-0012 refuses), so bootstrap had to — and did not. A real `bootstrap operator` plus `kubectl apply` of a Provider produced a binding pointing at a nonexistent role: a provider pod with zero permissions while the install reported success. The kind e2e surfaced it because a STALE copy of the role lingered from an earlier deploy — exactly how this would bite a real upgrade.
bugs.fix: build_operator_install now pushes InstallRole::Provider(backend).cluster_role() for every compiled-in backend, hard-erroring (naming the backend and expected path) when a manifest is missing. make kind-deploy-operator applies deploy/provider-*/rbac/clusterrole.yaml via glob. Guarded by operator_install_ships_the_shared_cluster_role_each_backend_needs and the_installed_cluster_role_name_matches_what_the_binding_references.

bugs.error_message: a real maintainer hostname survived the scrub, inside the changelog entry documenting the scrub
bugs.root_cause: The scrub removed the hostname from live_libvirtd.rs and the Makefile, then named the removed value in the changelog's 'Changed' list. rules/no-real-infrastructure.md lists the changelog explicitly, but a scrub naturally writes 'X -> Y' and X is the thing being scrubbed.
bugs.fix: Rewrote the entry as 'a real maintainer hostname -> bar.foo.io'. When recording a scrub, describe the removed value, never quote it.

bugs.error_message: target_pools() would return a pool named "" from a blank or trailing-comma pools attribute
bugs.root_cause: The filter dropping empty split segments was never asserted on. An import Job targeting pool "" fails on the libvirt host rather than at the reconciler, where the cause would be obvious.
bugs.fix: Added blank_entries_in_the_pools_attribute_are_dropped covering "", trailing comma, and an interior blank. Found by mutation testing, not by any failing test.

bugs.error_message: the caBundle UTF-8 check was pinned by no test at all
bugs.root_cause: The check lived inside read_secret_key, reachable only through a kube API call, so no unit test could touch it. Deleting it entirely kept the suite green — a binary DER value would have reached the TLS stack and failed with a far less obvious message.
bugs.fix: Extracted pem_from_secret_value() as a pure function and tested both the PEM and DER paths. Found by mutation testing.

bugs.error_message: error: can be more succinctly written as a byte str (clippy::byte_char_slices) at xdr_tests.rs:226
bugs.root_cause: Test used [b'a', b'b', b'c'] array literal; clippy::byte-char-slices (deny warnings) flags it as byte-string syntax is terser.
bugs.fix: Replaced with let bytes = *b"abc"; cargo clippy -p banlieue-libvirt --all-targets passes.

bugs.error_message: Semgrep code-scanning alerts rust.lang.security.temp-dir.temp-dir at import_tests.rs:126 and :151 (PR #7)
bugs.root_cause: Tests built scratch dirs via std::env::temp_dir() with a PID-based name, which Semgrep flags as a predictable path in a shared directory.
bugs.fix: Switched both tests to tempfile::tempdir() (auto-cleanup on drop), dropped manual create_dir_all/remove_dir_all, added tempfile = "3" dev-dependency. clippy clean, 23/23 import tests pass.

bugs.error_message: two providers reconciling one VMImage silently erase each other's status.perProvider rows and conditions
bugs.root_cause: status.perProvider and status.conditions are plain arrays with no x-kubernetes-list-type, so server-side apply treats them as ATOMIC: the whole array is owned by one field manager. Each provider applies the full list containing only its own rows, with force(), so it takes ownership and discards the other's. Reproduced on a real apiserver (kind): after vsphere then libvirt applied, perProvider was ['kvm-1'] only and conditions held only libvirt's. rawDiskArtifact survived because it is a distinct key with skip_serializing_if. examples/04-vmimage-ubuntu.yaml ships vsphere+proxmox+libvirt sources, so this is the documented case, not a corner.
bugs.fix: FIXED (ADR-0015). (1) status.perProvider gets x-kubernetes-list-type=map keyed on [providerName, providerNamespace]; status.conditions gets list-type=map keyed on [type], via #[schemars(extend(...))] in banlieue-api. (2) Providers no longer write VMImage.status.conditions at all — a provider cannot compute 'ready everywhere' from rows it does not own. (3) banlieue-controller gains a VMImage reconciler owning the aggregate Ready under field manager banlieue.io/controller. Verified on kind: perProvider now reads ['vc-1','kvm-1'] and a provider's later write neither duplicates its own row nor disturbs the controller's condition.

bugs.error_message: e2e `a_paused_class_suspends_its_providers` timed out after 120s waiting for the workload to appear once the ProviderClass was unpaused
bugs.root_cause: The skip path (Provider or ProviderClass paused) returned requeue_long() = 300s. Nothing watches ProviderClass — mapping a class back to its Providers needs an async lookup kube's synchronous watch mapper cannot do without a reflector store — so a paused Provider is only re-examined when that timer fires. Un-pausing therefore took up to FIVE MINUTES to take effect, with no event in between to shorten it. Not a correctness bug (it converges) but a bad enough UX bug that an operator would reasonably conclude un-pausing was broken.
bugs.fix: Return requeue_default() (30s) on the skip path instead. Checking a paused resource is a cheap no-op — two API reads and an early return — so the longer interval bought nothing and cost responsiveness. Proper follow-up is a reflector store so ProviderClass edits trigger affected Providers immediately, which would also remove the 30s lag on class image edits.

bugs.error_message: error: context "kind-banlieue-dev" does not exist — make kind-e2e failed at kind-create
bugs.root_cause: The kind workflow was only half-scoped to its own kubeconfig. `kind-e2e` ran the test with KUBECONFIG=$(KIND_KUBECONFIG), but all 24 other kubectl invocations used bare `kubectl --context kind-$(KIND_CLUSTER_NAME)`, which resolves against whatever $KUBECONFIG is selected. If that file lacks the context — which it did, because the cluster had been created under a different selected kubeconfig — every deploy step fails. The mirror-image hazard is worse: `kind create cluster` WRITES its context into the selected kubeconfig, so running the local e2e while pointed at the homelab config would have mutated that file.
bugs.fix: Added KIND_KUBECTL = kubectl --kubeconfig $(KIND_KUBECONFIG) --context kind-$(KIND_CLUSTER_NAME) and routed all 24 call sites through it; kind-create now runs `kind create` under KUBECONFIG=$(KIND_KUBECONFIG) and always refreshes that file before anything reads it. Verified: `make kind-e2e` passes and kind-banlieue-dev never appears in the default kubeconfig's contexts.

bugs.error_message: imagebuilder hot-deleted every OSArtifact every pass (owned=false on its own artifacts); ~7000 reconciles in 4 min, then a tracing-subscriber panic killed the process
bugs.root_cause: kube's DynamicObject parses `metadata` into the typed `metadata` field and OUT of the flattened `data` Value, so `obj.data["metadata"]["ownerReferences"]` is always Null. The SEC-005 staleness check read ownerReferences from `data`, making owner_uid_matches permanently false; the reconcile then deleted and recreated the artifact on every watch event.
bugs.fix: Read `obj.metadata.owner_references` (typed) instead; owner_uid_matches now takes Option<&[OwnerReference]>. Verified on kind: owned artifacts survive, forged/stale ones are still deleted.
bugs.learning: With kube's DynamicObject, never read metadata from `.data` — apiVersion/kind/spec/status live there, metadata does not. Any DynamicObject metadata check must go through the typed `.metadata` field.

bugs.error_message: namespaces "banlieue-imagebuild" not found — banlieue-imagebuilder error-loops immediately after the documented install
bugs.root_cause: The imagebuilder defaulted --build-namespace to banlieue-imagebuild, but `banlieue bootstrap imagebuilder` only ever creates banlieue-system. The documented install path therefore produced a deployment that could never reconcile.
bugs.fix: PARTIAL — default changed to banlieue-system so the namespace exists, but see the PodSecurity finding: banlieue-system enforces restricted and kairos build pods need privileged, so the build namespace must ultimately be separate AND created by bootstrap with appropriate labels.

bugs.error_message: imagebuilder and libvirt provider disagreed on --build-namespace (banlieue-imagebuild vs banlieue-system)
bugs.root_cause: Two crates, each internally consistent, disagreeing on a shared contract. The imagebuilder creates the artifacts PVC in its build namespace; the provider mounts that PVC into an import Job in ITS build namespace. A PVC cannot be mounted across namespaces — ADR-0010 says so in a comment — so the import could never work. Neither crate's tests could see it; only the binary crate links both.
bugs.fix: Added a cross-crate contract test in crates/banlieue/src/cli_tests.rs asserting the two defaults are equal, and aligned them. The test is the durable part: the correct VALUE is still open pending the PodSecurity decision.

bugs.error_message: osartifacts.build.kairos.io is forbidden: cannot create resource "osartifacts" — every OSArtifact creation 403d
bugs.root_cause: The ClusterRole granted get/list/watch/patch/delete on osartifacts but NOT create, with a comment asserting that 'patch covers server-side apply (create-or-update in one call)'. That is false: SSA is a patch when the object exists and a CREATE when it does not. The imagebuilder's entire purpose is creating OSArtifacts, so nothing worked.
bugs.fix: Added `create`. Added a bootstrap test asserting that any role which server-side-applies an object also holds create on it — the general form of the mistake.

bugs.error_message: kairos build pod rejected: violates PodSecurity "restricted:latest": privileged, allowPrivilegeEscalation, unrestricted capabilities, runAsNonRoot, seccompProfile
bugs.root_cause: ADR-0010 named a --build-namespace but never said what it must PERMIT. kairos-operator's OSArtifact builder needs privileged:true for loop devices; privileged is denied by `baseline` as well as `restricted`, so the hosting namespace must enforce `privileged` (no admission floor). Pointing the build at banlieue-system would have removed that floor from the controller, the operator (an RBAC grantor) and every per-backend provider pod.
bugs.fix: ADR-0016: dedicated banlieue-imagebuild namespace with enforce=privileged and audit/warn=restricted; both components default --build-namespace there; bootstrap creates it. NOTE the split bounds admission surface, NOT escape capability — a privileged pod escapes to its node regardless of namespace; node isolation is tracked as the outstanding complementary control.

bugs.error_message: namespaces created by `banlieue bootstrap` carried no PodSecurity labels at all
bugs.root_cause: build_namespace() set only app.kubernetes.io/name, while deploy/controller/namespace.yaml sets enforce/audit/warn=restricted. The documented CLI install path (ADR-0013) therefore produced a LESS hardened cluster than the manifest path, and no test covered it. This silently voided ADR-0016's core premise, which is that banlieue-system is restricted.
bugs.fix: build_namespace() now applies enforce/audit/warn=restricted; added build_imagebuild_namespace() with enforce=privileged + audit/warn=restricted; four tests pin both postures and assert the two namespaces are distinct.

bugs.error_message: MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "creds": secret "libvirt-creds" not found — import pods stuck in ContainerCreating
bugs.root_cause: The import Job manifest mounted the Provider's credentials Secret as a volume. The Secret lives with the Provider (banlieue-system); the Job runs in the build namespace (ADR-0016). A volume mount cannot cross namespaces, exactly like the PVC. ADR-0016 §4 designed cross-namespace RBAC for API READS of the Secret but I missed that the manifest also mounted it.
bugs.fix: Removed the volume and mount entirely — they were vestigial. import.rs never read the mounted path; it resolves credentials through the Kubernetes API via credentials::resolve, which the ADR-0016 §4 RBAC already permits. Strictly better: the Secret is no longer projected into the filesystem of a pod running in a namespace with no admission floor. Test now asserts NO secret is projected.

bugs.error_message: operator created the import Role/RoleBinding then immediately deleted them: 'pruned workload object no longer part of this Provider', in a loop
bugs.root_cause: prune_namespaced() took `keep: Option<&str>` — a SINGLE name. One Provider legitimately owns two Roles now: the controller's and the import identity's (ADR-0016 §4). The import objects carry the provider labels, so the pruner matched them, found their names != the one kept name, and deleted them on every reconcile. Create -> prune -> create -> prune.
bugs.fix: prune_namespaced() now takes `keep: &[String]`; the Role/RoleBinding call sites pass both the workload name and its `-import` sibling. The teardown path passes an empty slice so deletion still removes everything.

bugs.error_message: gen-raw-efi-disk (error: open /dev/loop1: no such file or directory) — kairos build failed on Hadron Linux nodes
bugs.root_cause: Recurrence of bug-098 in a new guise. The loop MODULE was loaded and /dev/loop0+loop1 existed at inspection time, but max_loop=0 means the kernel creates loop devices ON DEMAND. A privileged container only inherits device nodes that existed at container-creation time, so the build container started before loop1 existed and could never see it. The previous fix lived in the Debian cloud-init, which the Hadron rebuild discarded.
bugs.fix: Pre-created /dev/loop0..loop7 on the build node via a one-shot privileged pod (mknod b 7 N). Build then succeeded. NOT PERSISTENT — lost on reboot. Persistent fix belongs in the Kairos cloud-config: /etc/modules-load.d/loop.conf plus /etc/modprobe.d/loop.conf with `options loop max_loop=8`.

bugs.error_message: import pods Pending: 0/4 nodes available: 1 node had untolerated taint, 3 nodes didn't match PersistentVolume's node affinity
bugs.root_cause: Build scheduling was given to banlieue-imagebuilder but never reached the provider, so its import Jobs carried no nodeSelector or toleration. With node-local storage the artifacts PV is pinned to the node the build ran on — the tainted build node — so the only node that could mount it was the one the Job could not tolerate.
bugs.fix: The operator now forwards --build-node-selector/--build-toleration to every provider workload (new operator CLI flags -> Context -> build_args). Tests assert both that the flags are forwarded and that they are OMITTED when unset, since clap rejects empty values.

bugs.error_message: ImagePullBackOff: ghcr.io/firestoned/banlieue:v0.1.0: not found — every import Job
bugs.root_cause: The provider's --import-image defaulted to the released tag ghcr.io/firestoned/banlieue:v0.1.0 and nothing overrode it, so a provider running :local-dev spawned Jobs referencing a tag that does not exist. Version skew by construction: the Job runs the SAME binary as the provider, so it must run the same image.
bugs.fix: The operator now passes --import-image with the resolved ProviderClass image. Test asserts the flag matches the image the provider itself runs.

bugs.error_message: build scheduling could not be set through `banlieue bootstrap` — it had to be patched onto Deployments by hand after install
bugs.root_cause: The imagebuilder and operator both grew --build-node-selector/--build-toleration, but InstallRole::args() returned a fixed vec per role, so the installer could not pass them. The documented install path therefore produced a cluster where privileged build pods could be scheduled onto control-plane nodes — the exact thing ADR-0016's follow-up exists to prevent.
bugs.fix: InstallOptions carries both; InstallRole::args_with(opts) appends them for Operator and Imagebuilder only. Tests assert the controller does NOT receive them (it does not declare the flags and would fail to start) and that unset emits nothing (clap rejects empty values).

bugs.error_message: DESIGN ERROR (caught in review, not by a test): import Jobs were given a nodeSelector pinning them to the build node
bugs.root_cause: I generalised from local-path being installed on the test cluster and concluded the import Job 'must land on the build node', then propagated a nodeSelector through the operator to enforce it. Kubernetes already solves this: the Job mounts the artifacts PVC and the scheduler honours the bound PV's own nodeAffinity. The evidence was in the failure message all along -- '3 node(s) didn't match PersistentVolume's node affinity' shows the scheduler had already applied it; only the TAINT excluded the remaining node. The selector was redundant on node-local storage and actively wrong on network-attached storage, where it would pin a Job to a node it has no reason to be on.
bugs.fix: Import Jobs carry NO nodeSelector; placement follows the PVC. Tolerations are kept, reframed as permission-to-land rather than placement. The operator forwards only tolerations. Node selection remains for the BUILD pod, where it is a genuine policy decision (privileged, ADR-0016). ADR-0016 and the SDK docs corrected.

bugs.error_message: the loop-device cloud-config would have been silently ignored: `files:` was written as a STAGE NAME
bugs.root_cause: In Kairos/yip, `files:` is a property of a stage STEP, not a stage of its own. I added it as a sibling of `after-install:` and `boot:` under `stages:`, creating a bogus stage named 'files' whose entries carry path/permissions/content where a step expects name/commands/files. yip has no such stage, so nothing would ever have been written — and nothing would have errored either.
bugs.fix: Moved the `files:` block inside the boot stage's step, alongside its `commands:`. Confirmed the surrounding shell still parses.

bugs.error_message: after a power cut and node reboot, /dev/loop1..7 were gone again — only loop-control and loop0 remained
bugs.root_cause: The manual mknod applied to unblock the first build was never persistent, and the running nodes were installed BEFORE the cloud-config fix, so they carry neither the modprobe.d parameter nor the modules-load.d entry. An unplanned host power loss demonstrated this within hours.
bugs.fix: Wrote /etc/modules-load.d/banlieue-loop.conf and /etc/modprobe.d/banlieue-loop.conf into the node's persistent /etc via a privileged pod, plus recreated the device nodes for the running kernel. Nodes built from the corrected cloud-config get this at install time.

bugs.error_message: images were imported into every pool on the host, including one the admin never declared (3 GiB written into `boot`)
bugs.root_cause: target_pools() read status.failureDomains[].attributes.raw['pools'], which is DISCOVERY output — every pool libvirtd reports. The declared capability list is spec.capabilities.storageClasses, verified into attributes.availableStorageClasses. On the homelab Provider three classes were declared (default, images, k0s-bootstrap) but four pools exist, so every import also wrote a full copy into `boot`. Contradicts non-negotiable #4: capabilities are declared, discovery is a status-time concern.
bugs.fix: target_pools() now maps declared storageClasses -> target['pool'], filtered to classes present in availableStorageClasses (i.e. verified on the host), and deduplicated via BTreeSet because two classes may map to one pool and would otherwise run the same multi-gigabyte transfer twice, racing each other. Removed the now-meaningless test that parsed raw['pools'].

bugs.error_message: Grype code-scanning alerts (11 CVEs) stay open even though curated .vex/*.json statements exist and the CI grype job passes --vex
bugs.root_cause: CI pins GRYPE_VERSION=0.87.0, which silently ignores --vex: findings with matching VEX statements are still emitted to SARIF (verified by scanning the published image with 0.87.0 +/- VEX — identical 11 results). grype 0.115.0/0.118.0 filter correctly.
bugs.fix: Bump GRYPE_VERSION to 0.118.0 in build.yaml (plus distroless base digest bump in Dockerfile to clear libssl3t64 CVEs the newer schema-6 DB flags). Verified 0.118.0 filters all 8 curated VEX CVEs when scanning from the registry.

bugs.error_message: Invalid ref: f7dd8c54c2067bafc12ca7a55595d5ee9b75204a. Expected ref of the form refs/tags/vX.Y.Z (SLSA Provenance / generator exit 2, final job exit 27)
bugs.root_cause: The blanket SHA-pinning sweep (041f34b, 2026-08-13) rewrote the slsa-github-generator reusable workflow reference to a commit digest. The generator reads the ref it was called with as its own BUILDER_REF and only accepts refs/tags/vX.Y.Z release tags, so it aborted before generating provenance; the downstream 'final' and artifact-upload steps then failed with 127 / 'Input required and not supplied: path'.
bugs.fix: Reverted that single uses: back to @v2.1.0 and added an inline comment forbidding future digest pinning of this reference. All other actions stay SHA-pinned.

bugs.error_message: 31 open Grype code-scanning alerts on glibc/libc6/zlib1g; auto-vex-reachability emitting 0 statements
bugs.root_cause: The CVE->symbol map was committed as a scaffold ('Scaffold only -- no entries yet'), so the reachability tool had nothing to match and silently emitted zero statements every run. The tool worked; its input was empty. Separately Dockerfile.chainguard's digest had drifted to glibc 2.43-r6 while fixes existed at 2.43-r7/r10.
bugs.fix: Populated the map with 12 CVEs. Key insight: list the advisory's PUBLIC entry points, not the internal function it names -- parse_tilde/gz_vacate never appear in a dynsym table, so map them to wordexp/glob and gzprintf/gzwrite. Verified all 96 symbols absent from the release binary's 154 undefined dynsym entries before claiming not_affected. Bumped Chainguard base to glibc 2.44-r5.

bugs.error_message: Scorecard: Project is vulnerable to GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq (uuid@9.0.1)
bugs.root_cause: linkinator 6.1.2 -> gaxios -> uuid@^9. The caret ceiling at 9.x meant no npm override could reach the fixed 11.1.1; the dependency had to go, not be pinned.
bugs.fix: Bumped linkinator to 8.1.0, which replaced gaxios with undici and pulls neither gaxios nor uuid (26 packages total, npm audit clean). Needs Node >=22, satisfied by the runner default; recorded in docs.yaml.

bugs.error_message: Unpinned third-party container in CI: 'image: returntocorp/semgrep' (no tag) and .clusterfuzzlite/Dockerfile unmanaged by Dependabot
bugs.root_cause: The Semgrep job container had no tag (implicitly :latest) in the deprecated returntocorp namespace, running with the repo checkout and security-events: write. Separately dependabot's docker ecosystem used directory: '/' which only scans the repo root, so .clusterfuzzlite/Dockerfile was never covered.

bugs.error_message: TlsIdentity derived Debug would print client_key_pem (the libvirt mTLS private key) into any {:?} / log line

bugs.error_message: kind-e2e-dry-run: no matches for kind "ProviderClass" in version "banlieue.io/v1alpha1" ... ensure CRDs are installed first; Error from server (NotFound): namespaces "banlieue-system" not found
bugs.root_cause: When the e2e was split into per-suite CI jobs, kind-e2e-dry-run (ex kind-verify-dry-run) had its prerequisite relaxed from the bootstrap install to a bare kind cluster, to make that job cheap. But `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` PERSISTS NOTHING: the Namespace and CRDs carried in the same manifest stream never actually exist, so every later object that depends on them fails to map or 404s. The old target only ever worked because it always ran AFTER kind-bootstrap-install in the same recipe.
bugs.fix: kind-e2e-dry-run: kind-bootstrap-install (not kind-kubeconfig), with a recipe comment spelling out why a bare cluster cannot work, so it is not 'optimised' back. Same reasoning already applied to kind-e2e-escape-hatch, whose `bootstrap provider` has creates_namespace: false.

bugs.error_message:
Parse error on line 27: ...sible to sizing;
they only count aga -----------------------^ Expecting 'NEWLINE', ',', '()', 'SOLID_OPEN_ARROW', ... got 'INVALID'
bugs.root_cause: A semicolon inside sequence-diagram MESSAGE TEXT is a parse error: mermaid's sequence lexer treats ';' as a statement separator, so `A->>B: did x; then y` ends the statement mid-sentence and the remainder is INVALID. Introduced while avoiding parentheses in participant aliases by swapping them for semicolons -- trading an imagined syntax risk for a real one. Notes and flowchart labels are unaffected; only sequence message/note text after the colon.
bugs.fix: Use a comma or an em dash instead of ';' in sequence text. Verify by extracting every ```mermaid fence and rendering it: awk into diag-NN.mmd, then `mmdc -i diag-NN.mmd -o diag-NN.svg` (PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 plus PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH pointed at the installed Chrome avoids the chromium download, with {"args":["--no-sandbox"]} in a -p config).

bugs.error_message: `make docs` exits 0 while a page shows a mermaid error box in the browser
bugs.root_cause: mkdocs NEVER validates mermaid. pymdownx.superfences only rewrites the ```mermaid fence into <div class="mermaid">; the actual parse happens client-side in mermaid.min.js loaded via extra_javascript. So a syntactically broken diagram is invisible to the docs build -- and to CI, which runs the same build. `make docs` is also not --strict, so a broken internal link does not fail it either.
bugs.fix: Treat a green docs build as proof of nothing about diagrams. Render each fence with @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli locally before committing (see bug-143), and check new links resolve by hand until the build gains --strict.

bugs.error_message: Guest never boots from a .qcow2 backing volume: no console, no DHCP lease, no qemu-guest-agent. live_guest.rs reports "no qemu-guest-agent AND no network address within 300s".
bugs.root_cause: ensure_disks() passed the CONSTANT BANLIEUE_BACKING_FORMAT ("raw") to qcow2_overlay_volume_xml instead of calling backing_format(&source.name), which exists, is documented, and is unit-tested -- but was never called. libvirt deliberately does not probe a backing file's format, so it accepts <format type='raw'/> over a qcow2 image without complaint; QEMU then presents the qcow2 header to the guest as its partition table and nothing boots. Hidden twice over: backing_format is `pub`, so no dead-code warning, and the test named `an_immediate_machine_declares_its_backing_format` asserted only that a volume with the right NAME was created -- FakeMachineClient discarded the XML, making the fake more permissive than libvirt. The pool/claim e2e also missed it because it uses readiness InfrastructureReady, which fires when the domain is running, not when the guest booted.
bugs.fix: Call backing_format(&source.name) at the call site. FakeMachineClient now keeps created_volume_xml so a test can assert the document, and both tests (qcow2 and raw backing) check the declared <format>. Rule: a fake that discards what the real system parses will hide exactly the bug the test is named for.

bugs.error_message: probe_guest returns AgentUnreachable for a healthy guest whose marker simply does not exist yet: "expected NotAnnounced for a reachable agent with no marker, got AgentUnreachable".
bugs.root_cause: probe_guest assumed libvirtd delivers an agent-level error as an Ok payload carrying JSON ("An Ok reply -- even one carrying a JSON error -- means it did [answer]"). It does not: virDomainQemuAgentCommand turns a QMP error into an RPC fault, so call_on_program returns Err. guest-file-open on a missing /run/banlieue/phase is therefore indistinguishable from a missing agent, and both fell into the Ok(None)|Err(_) arm. probe_guest had NO unit tests at all -- guest_tests.rs covers only the pure command-building and parsing helpers -- so the wrong model was never challenged offline, and the tri-state that ADR-0043 Decision 8 relies on for its requeue cadence was inverted for the entire install window of every Deferred member.
bugs.fix: On a failed open, ask guest-ping to classify: ping OK => NotAnnounced, otherwise AgentUnreachable. Costs one extra round trip, paid only on the negative path. Added guest_ping_cmd() and classify_open_failure(); verified live in live_guest.rs, which now asserts both NotAnnounced (marker absent) and Installed (marker written through the agent).

bugs.error_message: A CALM flow's rendered mermaid diagram silently fails to draw: `t1["1. ... kubectl patch providerclass vsphere -p '{"spec":{"image":{"tag":"v0.2.0"}}}'`"]`
bugs.root_cause: The Handlebars template wraps every flow transition description in a quoted mermaid node label, t1["..."]. A DOUBLE QUOTE anywhere in that description therefore terminates the label early and the remainder is parsed as graph syntax. flow-upgrade-provider-fleet embedded a kubectl patch with four quote pairs and had been failing to render on the published site. Nothing caught it: `make calm-validate` checks architecture.json against the CALM meta-schema and knows nothing about the rendered output, and mkdocs never parses mermaid at all (superfences just emits a div; mermaid.min.js parses client-side in the browser).
bugs.fix: Never put a double quote in a CALM node/relationship/flow description -- use prose or single quotes. After `make calm-diagrams`, render every generated fence before committing: awk the ```mermaid blocks out of docs/src/architecture/{flows,system}.md into diag-NN.mmd and run mmdc on each (PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 + PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH at the installed Chrome, with {"args":["--no-sandbox"]} via -p). A one-liner audit for the specific defect: extract the fences and flag any label whose text contains more than one quote.

bugs.error_message: Docs-only PRs block forever: 4 required checks never report
bugs.root_cause: build.yaml carried a workflow-level `paths:` filter, so a PR touching only docs/ or .github/community/ never triggered it. Four of the six required status checks come from that workflow, and a required check that never reports leaves the PR pending indefinitely. No bypass actors exist (deliberately - Scorecard penalises admin bypass). Roadmap 16's own recorded fix ('add a required-checks job with if: always()') was insufficient for the same reason: a workflow-level paths filter stops the whole workflow, aggregator job included, so the PR would block on one pending context instead of four.
bugs.fix: Removed the paths: filter from the pull_request trigger so build.yaml always runs and always reports. Added a `changes` job calling `make ci-code-changed` (path list lives in the Makefile, testable locally, no inline workflow logic) and gated format/clippy/extract-version/security/cargo-deny on it; test/docker/package-deploy-manifests skip transitively via extract-version. license-check and verify-commits are never gated. Added `required-checks` (if: always(), needs the four plus those two) failing only on failure/cancelled - a skip is a pass. Ruleset must then require the single context instead of the four.

bugs.error_message: Kairos datasource: 'CIDATA devices to be checked: []' / 'no metadata/userdata found' with a CIDATA seed on virtio-blk; go-diskfs v1.7.0: 'unable to convert creation date/time from bytes: parsing time "0000-00-00T00:00:00.00+00:00": month out of range'
